name: APT36 Stage 1 - Renamed-Binary Parent Spawns PowerShell (T1204.002)
blast_radius: A copy of cmd.exe renamed winword.exe runs PowerShell to write one marker file. Microsoft Word is never opened; delivery (T1566.001) is not tested here.
telemetry: Sysmon EID 1: ParentImage named winword.exe, not the real Word binary
detection: EDR: process named winword.exe spawning powershell.exe where the real parent path does not match Office

name: APT36 Stage 2 - Document with a Remote Template Relationship (T1221)
blast_radius: Builds a .docx with an attachedTemplate relationship pointing at a loopback server, fetches the template over HTTP, and verifies the relationship target and the fetched bytes. Office is never opened, so template-triggered macro execution is not tested here.
telemetry: Sysmon EID 3: loopback connection to the template URL
Sysmon EID 11: .docx and template files created
detection: EDR: an OOXML relationship target pointing outside the document package

name: APT36 Stage 3 - Keyboard-Hook API Capability Probe (T1056.001)
blast_radius: Checks whether user32.dll (the SetWindowsHookEx surface) is loaded in the current process and whether any known security-vendor module is also loaded. No hook is installed and no keystroke is captured; a direct-mode result records this as a capability probe, not a scored technique.
telemetry: Sysmon EID 7: module load list of the probing process
detection: EDR: process capability survey preceding a SetWindowsHookEx call

name: APT36 Stage 4 - HKCU Run Key Persistence Write + Delete (T1547.001)
blast_radius: Writes one run-tagged value under HKCU Software Microsoft Windows CurrentVersion Run, reads it back, deletes it, then verifies the value is gone.
telemetry: Sysmon EID 13 and 14: registry value set and deleted under the Run key
detection: EDR: new HKCU Run value written by a script host

name: APT36 Stage 5 - DNS A-Record Beacon with Jitter (T1071.004)
blast_radius: Sends five DNS A queries roughly two seconds apart, each for a unique run-tagged name under the reserved .invalid domain. Telemetry mode: validates host DNS visibility only.
telemetry: Sysmon EID 22: DNS query events for the run-tagged names
detection: DNS analytics: periodic queries with high-entropy labels to one parent domain

name: APT36 Stage 6 - Scheduled Task Created, Run Once and Deleted (T1053.005)
blast_radius: Creates a one-time scheduled task with a run-tagged name whose action writes a marker file, runs it once, then deletes it and verifies deletion with a query.
detection: EDR: schtasks.exe /create from a script host
cleanup:
Get-ChildItem -Path $env:TEMP -Filter 'bas_a36_*' -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Remove-Item -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName 'bas_a36_*' -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Unregister-ScheduledTask -Confirm:$false -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

name: APT36 Stage 7 - mshta HTA Dropper Chain (T1218.005)
blast_radius: Runs mshta.exe on a run-tagged HTA whose VBScript starts cmd.exe through WScript.Shell, which writes one marker file.
telemetry: Sysmon EID 1: mshta.exe, then cmd.exe as its child
detection: EDR: mshta.exe spawning cmd.exe via WScript.Shell.Run

name: APT36 Stage 8 - regsvr32 Local JScript Scriptlet Chain (T1218.010)
blast_radius: Runs regsvr32.exe /u /i on a local .sct file whose JScript starts cmd.exe through WScript.Shell, the Squiblydoo pattern against a local file only (no remote fetch).
telemetry: Sysmon EID 1: regsvr32.exe /i: with a local .sct path
detection: EDR: regsvr32.exe loading scrobj.dll with /i: against a non-standard file

name: APT36 Stage 9 - DNS TXT Beacon (CrimsonRAT Channel Pattern) (T1071.004)
blast_radius: Sends four DNS TXT queries to run-tagged .invalid names, the record type CrimsonRAT uses for channel registration. Telemetry mode: validates host DNS visibility only.
telemetry: Sysmon EID 22: TXT-type DNS query events
detection: DNS analytics: TXT queries to names that never resolve

name: APT36 Stage 10 - Download Cradle with Hash Verification (T1105)
blast_radius: Fetches a payload from a loopback server through a hidden PowerShell child and verifies its SHA-256; the payload is never executed.
detection: EDR: download cradle landing an unexecuted binary in a temp path
